text:
maria: FYI found a new CVE affecting net/http's header parsing that can cause panic on malformed input. Observed in our auth-proxy logs, spike in 500s this morning.
kevin: link to advisory?
maria: https://example.cve.local/CVE-2024-XXXX - looks like golang.org/x/net/http2 and std net/http variants. Repro in staging with fuzz corpus.
sam: can you paste the minimal stack trace?
maria: "panic: runtime error: index out of range
net/http/xyz.go:123
...
proxy/handler.go:48"
vijay: OK, impact surface: auth-proxy, token-introspection, and any internal clients that accept untrusted headers. Is grpc affected too?
maria: grpc upstream uses http2 but preliminary tests show our grpc gateway isn't hitting the panic. Still need to test grpc-go v1.68+.
kevin: immediate mitigations: 1) temporary header length cap on proxy (env var) 2) pin go stdlib in builds? (we vendor)
alyssa: We don't pin stdlib; we vendor modules. The vuln is in stdlib/net and x/net. We should add a module replace to force x/net to patched tag.
sam: Could we roll a canary with header cap and new x/net patch to Dedicated first? Small % of traffic.
vijay: Also enable more verbose audit logging for header parsing failures so we can see if exploit attempts exist. Add a flag to log sanitized headers.
maria: adding KMS note: if we rotate keys as part of response plan, need to coordinate with infra for token signing keys. Not urgent but tracking.
kevin: action items: @sam to open PR with module replace for golang.org/x/net@v0.18.0-patch and net/http guard; @alyssa to prepare canary deployment config; @vijay to add audit logs and a dashboard.
sam: starting PR, will include test case from fuzz harness. Patch diff will be small - defensive index checks.
alyssa: canary plan: route 2% traffic to Dedicated pool, fallback after 10m errors >1%.
security-bot: New CVE ticket created: SEC-2024-0456. Assigned to eng-security.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued: canary-1729001234 by alyssa at 2024-06-18T10:12:00Z
vijay: Quick question on pinning: do we want a long-term policy to pin x/net minor releases in go.mod? Feels brittle but worth stability.
kevin: Prefer a targeted pin in go.mod with an entry and a comment linking to SEC ticket. We'll remove once stdlib release includes fix.
maria: Also need to update our vuln scanner rules to flag this CVE and any transitive x/net usage in customers' private deploy manifests.
sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/789 - includes test + module replace + header cap feature flag.
kevin: Reviewing now, will approve if CI green. After merge, schedule canary and rolling update.
alyssa: Postmortem owners? Recommend eng-security + auth-proxy team. I'll draft timeline.
maria: thanks all. If you see suspicious retries from 10.11.0.0/16, please escalate to oncall.
kevin: noting, will coordinate with infra for KMS rotations if token signing needs it.
